messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: @channel PAGING: Multiple CI pipelines failing with GitHub Actions / Packages errors. Detected elevated 429/503 when fetching packages and actions metadata. Creating incident INC-4810.
Lina G: seeing failures on github-hosted runners: jobs fail during `npm ci` and `actions/checkout` step. Example error: `GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/-/package/foo 429 Too Many Requests`
Ravi S: ack. which parts are impacted? builds, publishes, or both?
Tom H: both — pulls and publishes. Our nightly hotfix builds can't complete and publish images. GHCR publish attempts returning 503 for some pushes.
Lina G: paste of job log:
```
npm ERR! code E429
npm ERR! 429 Too Many Requests - GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/-/package/@redwood/infra
info Visit https://yarnpkg.com/en/docs/cli/install for documentation about this command.
error Command failed with exit code 429.
```
ops-bot: deploy/hotfix-2026 failed: 1/6 jobs failed at package-install. Retries disabled.
Ravi S: immediate mitigation brainstorm:
- try switching CI to pull from a mirror (verdaccio/artifactory) and point registry via `.npmrc`
- build artifacts locally and push container images directly to our ECR/GCR (bypass GHCR)
- use self-hosted runner pool (if runners have cached node_modules)
- delay non-critical deploys until GitHub recovers
Lina G: I'm spinning up a small verdaccio instance in prod VPC and will seed critical packages from our lockfile. Will share registry URL when ready.
Tom H: I'll start a manual build on a workstation, tag the image, and push to our ECR: `us-east-2.aws/rw/hotfix:hotfix-1967`
Elena F: I'm coordinating CS comms. Which customers are queued for the hotfix? CS-bot, list please.
CS-bot: flagged customers: payfast, media-hub, retail-pro. Draft message prepared.
Lina G: verdaccio up at `http://10.4.12.8:4873` and I've published three critical packages from tarballs in the repo. To use: add `.npmrc` with `registry=http://10.4.12.8:4873` before running `npm ci` in the CI job. Patching CI templates now.
Ravi S: great. note: GitHub Actions self-hosted runners are also intermittently failing when they try to talk to the Actions API for workflow dispatch (500). We should avoid workflow_dispatch triggers for now.
Tom H: manual image build complete and pushed to ECR. Smoke test on staging passed. Will queue manual rollout to canary.
Lina G: patched `r/deploy-hotfix` pipeline to use the internal registry and re-run job. Initial re-run succeeded for install step. Still failing on publish to ghcr.io (503).
ops-bot: r/deploy-hotfix re-run 2: 5/6 jobs succeeded, publish job failed -> ghcr push 503.
Elena F: sending proactive note to flagged customers: "We detected a GitHub Packages/Actions outage impacting our CI. We've applied an emergency workaround by building artifacts and pushing to our internal registry. Your patches are being deployed; we'll update once GitHub fully recovers."
Ravi S: assigning roles:
- Incident Owner: Lina G (temporary)
- Build lead: Tom H
- CI infra + runbook: Ravi S
- Customer comms: Elena F
- Postmortem: assigned to Lina G
ops-bot: PagerDuty INC-4810 assigned to Lina G (primary oncall)
Lina G: documenting mitigation steps in the incident doc. Also adding a short-term CI-run: `npm config set registry http://10.4.12.8:4873` in the pipeline template and creating a network ACL to allow runners access.
Tom H: rolling out manual canary to 5% traffic. Monitoring logs and errors.
Lina G: noted: some internal devs reported `401` when using GitHub token auth for packages, looks like token throttle/validation errors too. We should rotate any expiring tokens used by CI after incident.
Ravi S: next actions:
1) Keep verdaccio mirror seeded and CI patched (owner: Lina G)
2) Avoid workflow_dispatch triggers and long-run jobs until Actions stable (owner: Ravi S)
3) Use ECR/GCR for publishing emergency hotfix images (owner: Tom H)
4) CS messaging and status page update (owner: Elena F)
5) Postmortem and CI decoupling plan (owner: Lina G)
Lina G: GH status: https://www.githubstatus.com updated: "Some customers may experience errors with Packages and Actions" at 17:22 UTC. Marking incident Sev 2 due to blocked hotfix pipeline.
Tom H: canary shows no regressions; proceeding to 25% rollout.
CS-bot: customer notifications sent. responses: 2 customers asked for ETA; replied with current workaround and link to status page.
Ravi S: creating a short-lived runbook entry in infra repo: `docs/ci-github-outage.md` with instructions to stand up verdaccio, update `.npmrc`, and fallback publish targets. Will link from incident doc.
Lina G: handoff note for night oncall: I'll keep monitoring for 1 hour then hand to Elena F. If GitHub recovers, wait for full recovery of packages before re-enabling GHCR publishes to avoid duplicate image tags.
Elena F: ack. will take over at 19:30 UTC and continue monitoring. Drafting post-incident customer email template for CS review.
ops-bot: Incident INC-4810 status changed -> mitigation in progress. Last action logged at 17:48 UTC (last_message_ts 1967901899).
Tom H: final note — add a periodic artifact mirror for our top 50 packages and pre-publish base images to internal registries as part of CI hardening; include in postmortem action items.
Lina G: thanks team. Leaving incident open for postmortem, closing active mitigation work. :thumbsup:
